title: observability: token-level latency & cost metrics, dashboards, and alert tuning
author: Ethan Carter
description: Motivation: customers and internal SREs need token-level breakdowns for latency and cost to diagnose regressions and to tune batching and caching. This PR introduces per-token metrics, a set of Grafana dashboards for token-cost/latency analysis, and tuned alert rules to reduce noisy alerts while capturing meaningful regressions. Summary of changes: 1) ingest-level metrics: add token_latency_ms_per_position and token_cost_usd_per_position histograms and summaries with labels (model, route, region, customer_tier, position_bucket) so we can track head/mid/tail token behavior; 2) instrumentation: add lightweight sampling and aggregated tag propagation in the serving runtime to avoid high cardinality and performance impacts; 3) dashboards: new token_cost_latency dashboard with pre-computed panels for p50/p95/p99 by position bucket and by model and route; 4) alerts: tuned alert rules that fire on sustained token-p99 latency regressions or sudden cost-per-token increases, with automatic suppression during deploy windows; 5) docs and examples: observability runbook, example queries, and a notebook for slice analysis; 6) tests: unit tests for metric aggregation and integration tests for alert rule evaluation. Rollout plan: gradual rollout behind feature flag monitored for metric volume and performance, enable dashboards by default for SRE and Platform teams, and open to enterprise users via Console opt-in. Checklist: - [x] metric names reviewed with SRE - [x] dashboard mockups reviewed - [x] alerts tuned against historical data - [x] load testing for metric cardinality - [x] docs updated - [x] integration tests added

ci_checks: CI pipeline: unit-tests (pass), integration-tests (passed on rerun), lint (pass), e2e-grafana (pass), tsdb-cardinality-check (pass), performance-smoke (pass). Note: integration-tests failed once due to test ordering, rerun passed.
release_notes: Added token-level latency and cost metrics, Grafana dashboards for token cost/latency analysis, and tuned alert rules to surface token-p99 regressions and cost anomalies. Rollout behind feature flag; safe to enable for staging and SRE teams.
notes_for_ops: Feature guarded by feature flag 'token_metrics_v1'. Monitor metric ingest volume and tsdb cardinality. If metric volume spikes, disable flag and open incident. Alerts include deploy window suppression and a 30m burn-in delay after enabling.
testing_and_validation: Unit tests added for aggregation logic; integration tests validate alert firing using synthetic historical data; performance smoke showed <1% p50 latency impact at 1k rps with sampling enabled. Historical tuning used 12-week window (2025-11 to 2026-01).
egress_considerations: Metrics are aggregated server-side; only low-cardinality labels emitted. No customer PII included in metrics. Cost estimates: ~1.2M additional metric points/day at peak for full rollout; sampling reduces to ~150k/day.
maintainers: SRE Team (oncall rota), Observability Platform (Priya Nair)
impact_summary: Provides engineers and SREs with per-token visibility that enables targeted batching/KV-cache optimizations, faster incident triage for latency regressions, and more accurate token-level cost attribution.
user-facing_changes: New dashboards in Console under Observability > Token Cost & Latency. Enterprise customers can opt-in via Console feature flag. No API contract changes.
follow_up_work: 1) auto-suggest alert thresholds based on historical baselines (ENG-4201); 2) add per-customer token-cost chargeback exports (PM-118); 3) expand position buckets for long-tail analysis.
authors_notes: Deployed to staging and observed metric volume consistent with estimates. We validated alert suppression during deploy windows and adjusted the cooldown to 15 minutes after deploys. Reach out to obs-team with any dashboard feedback.
